from ohm's law
$\begin{aligned}
& V=I R \\
& \ln V=\ln I+\ln R \\
& \frac{\Delta V}{V}=\frac{\Delta I}{I}+\frac{\Delta R}{R} \\

& \left|\frac{\Delta R}{R}\right| \times 100=\frac{4}{100} \times 100=4 \%

The above is shown in the below figure, From parallelogram law, $\phi \ \text{ and } \theta$ is related as, $\tan (\phi)=\frac{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}| \sin (\theta)}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}| \cos (\theta)} \text{. }$ Substituting all the corresponding given values in above relation, we have, $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \tan \left(45^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=\frac{2 \sin \left(60^{{}^{\circ}}\right)}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|+2 \cos \left(60^{{}^{\circ}}\right)}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{a+1},(\because|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=a) \\ & \Rightarrow 1=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{a+1} \\ & \Rightarrow a+1=\sqrt{3} \\ & \Rightarrow a=\sqrt{3}-1 . \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A vector $\mathbf{P}$ directed along the $X$-axis is added to vector $\mathbf{Q}$ which has a magnitude of $10 \mathrm{ m}$. The resultant vector is directed along the $Y$-axis, with a magnitude that is 2 times that of $\mathbf{P}$. The magnitude of $\mathbf{P}$ is
questions.solution: By parallelogram law of vector addition, angle made by resultant with $\mathbf{P}$ is given by; $\tan \alpha=\frac{Q \sin \theta}{P+Q \cos \theta}$ Here $\alpha=90^{{}^{\circ}}$ so ; $\tan 90^{{}^{\circ}}=\infty=\frac{Q \sin \theta}{P+Q \cos \theta}\Rightarrow \quad P+Q \cos \theta=0$ or $Q \cos \theta=-P$ Now, magnitude of resultant, $R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2 P Q \cos \theta}$ Here, we have $R=2 P$ and $Q \cos \theta=-P$ and $Q=10 \mathrm{ m}$ So, $\quad 2 P=\sqrt{P^2+100-2 P^2}\Rightarrow \quad 4 P^2=100-P^2 \Rightarrow 5 P^2=100$ or $\quad P=\sqrt{20}=2 \sqrt{5} \mathrm{ m}$ Magnitude of $P$ is $2 \sqrt{5} \mathrm{ m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A physical quantity $P$ is related to four observables $a, b, c$ and $d$ as $P=\frac{\sqrt{a b} \cdot d^\alpha}{\sqrt{c}}(\alpha$ is constant) The percentage errors in $a, b, c$ and $d$ are $0.5 \%$ in each. If the percentage error in $P$ is $2 \%$, then $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
As, $P=\frac{a^{1 / 2} \cdot b^{1 / 2} \cdot d^\alpha}{c^{1 / 2}}$
So $\%$ error in $P=\frac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100\begin{aligned}
=\frac{1}{2} & \left(\frac{\Delta a}{a}\right) \times 100+\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\Delta b}{b} \times 100\right) \\
& +\alpha\left(\frac{\Delta d}{d} \times 100\right)+\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\Delta c}{c} \times 100\right)
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \%$ error in $P=\frac{1}{2} \times \%$ error in $a+\frac{1}{2} \times \%$ error in
$b+\frac{1}{2} \times \%$ error in $c+\alpha \times \%$ error in $d$
Now given,
\% Error in $P=2 \%\%$ Error in $a=\%$ error in $b=\%$ Error in $c=\%$ error in $d=0.5 \%$
Substituting these values in Eq. (i), we get
$\begin{aligned}
2 & =\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5+\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5+\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5+\alpha \times 0.5 \\
\Rightarrow 2 & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}+\alpha\right) \Rightarrow 4=\frac{3}{2}+\alpha
\end{aligned}
or \alpha=4-\frac{3}{2}=\frac{5}{2}\therefore \alpha$ is $5 / 2$.

questions.q: Two position vectors are given by $\overrightarrow{r_1}=(1,1,1)$ and $\overrightarrow{r_2}=(1,-1,1)$. The unit vector in the direction of $\overrightarrow{r_1} \times \overrightarrow{r_2}$
questions.solution:
We have
$\begin{aligned}
& \overline{\mathrm{r}_1} \times \overline{\mathrm{r}_2}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{\mathrm{i}} & \hat{\mathrm{j}} & \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
1 & 1 & 1 \\
1 & -1 & 1
\end{array}\right| \\
& =\hat{\mathrm{i}}(2)+\hat{\mathrm{j}}(0)+\hat{\mathrm{k}}(-2)=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}
\end{aligned}$
So, unit vector in the direction of
$\left(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}_1} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}_2}\right)=\frac{2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{\sqrt{2^2+(-2)^2}}=\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{\hat{\mathrm{k}}}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: The component of a vector $\mathbf{P}=3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}$ alog the direction $(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j})$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathbf{P}=3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}$ Let $Q=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}$
The component of $\mathbf{P}$ along the $\mathbf{Q}$ is given as $|\mathbf{P}| \cos \theta$ Hence, we know that, $\mathbf{P} \cdot \mathbf{Q}=|\mathbf{P}||\mathbf{Q}| \cos \theta\Rightarrow|P| \cos \theta=\frac{\mathbf{P} \cdot \mathbf{Q}}{|\mathbf{Q}|}=\frac{(3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}) \cdot(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j})}{\sqrt{1^2+2^2}}=\frac{3+8}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{11}{\sqrt{5}}$

questions.q: If two vectors $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are mutually perpendicular, then the component of $\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}$ along the direction of $\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B}$ is
questions.solution:
The two vectors $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are mutually perpendicular to each other
A. $\mathbf{B}=0\Rightarrow \quad A B \cos \theta=0\Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta=0 \Rightarrow \theta=90^{{}^{\circ}}|\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}|\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{A^2+B^2-2 A B \cos 90^{{}^{\circ}}} \\ & =\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\end{aligned}$
Unit vector along $\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}=\frac{\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}|}=\frac{\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}}{\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}$
component of $(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B})$ in direction of $(\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B})$ will be given as,
$=\frac{(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B}) \cdot(\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B})}{|\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}|}=\frac{\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{A}-\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}+\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{B}}{\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}=\frac{A^2-B^2}{\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}=\frac{|\mathbf{A}|^2-|\mathbf{B}|^2}{\sqrt{|\mathbf{A}|^2+|\mathbf{B}|^2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force $\overset{→}{F1}$ of magnitude $4N$ acts on an object of mass $1$ kg at origin in a direction $30 °$ above the positive $x$- axis. A second force $\overset{→}{F2}$ of magnitude $4N$ acts on the same object in the direction of the positive $y$- axis. The magnitude of the acceleration of the object is nearly
questions.solution:
Using parallelogram law of vector addition,

Resultant force acting on object is ${F}_{R} = \sqrt{{F}_{1}^{2} + {F}_{2}^{2} + 2{F}_{1}{F}_{2}cos\theta}$, here, $\theta = 90 ° - 30 ° = 60 °$ is angle between the forces.

Putting the values, we have

${F}_{R} = \sqrt{{4}^{2} + {4}^{2} + 2\left(4\right)\left(4\right)cos60 °} = 6. 9N$

Acceleration of the object is $a = \dfrac{FR}{m} = \dfrac{6. 9}{1} = 6. 9ms^{- 2}$.

Dot/Scalar product of two vectors gives scalar result. Cross/Vector product will give vector result.

Case:& $\left(\overset{→}{A} \cdot \overset{→}{A}\right) \left(\overset{→}{B} \cdot \overset{→}{C}\right)

Both left & right part will be a scalar value$ and hence its product will also be a scalar value.

Both left and $right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo dot product and the result will be a scalar value.

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo cross product and the result will be a vector value.

Case: $\overset{→}{A} \times $\left(\overset{→}{B} \times \overset{→}{C}\right)$

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo cross product and the result will be a vector value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If ${N}_{A}, {N}_{B}$ and ${N}_{C}$ are the number of significant figures in $A = 0. 001204m, B = 43120000m$, and $C = 1. 200m$& respectively then
questions.solution:
Significant figures are calculated through certain rules:

(i) All the digits that have no zero are significant.&

(ii)& Zeros that are written at the right hand side of the last non-zero digit in a number with the decimal are significant, while if the decimal is not present then the zeros are not significant.&

(iii)& The zeros that are written before non-zero digits are not significant.&

(iv) Zeros that are written between the non- zero digits are significant.&

So, here number of significant figures in $A$, $B$ and $C$ are four. Thus, ${N}_{A} = {N}_{B} = {N}_{C}$.

questions.q: Find the angle between the vectors $\mathbf{A}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{B}=4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$.
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathbf{A}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{B}=4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\mathbf{A} and \mathbf{B}$.
By using dot product,
$\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}=A B \cos \theta \text{, }$
where, $A and B$ are magnitudes of $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ respectively.
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
& A=\sqrt{2^2+4^2+4^2}=6 \\
& B=\sqrt{4^2+2^2+(-4)^2}=6
\end{aligned}$
Substituting the values, in dot product, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& (2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \cdot(4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})=(6)(6) \cos \theta \\
& 8+8-16=36 \cos \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta=90^{{}^{\circ}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: For the resultant of two vectors $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ to maximum, the angle between them should be
questions.solution:
We know that, the magnitude of resultant of two vectors $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$,
$R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2 A B \cos \theta}$
Here, $R \rightarrow R_{\max }$, when $\cos \theta$ is maximum
i.e. $\cos \theta=1\theta=0^{{}^{\circ}}$
Now, we get
$\begin{aligned} R_{\max } & =\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2 A B} \\ & =A+B\end{aligned}Hence, the $resultant is maximum when angle between two vectors is 0^{{}^{\circ}}$.$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an experiment, four quantities $a, b, c, d$ are measured with percentage errors 2\%, $1 \%, 3 \%$ and 5\%, respectively. Quantity $P$ is measured as $P=\frac{a^2 b^2}{c d}$. Find the percentage error in measuring $P$.
questions.solution:
Given, $\%$ error in $a, b, c and d$ are $2 \%, 1 \%, 3 \% and 5 \%$, respectively, and $P=\frac{a^2 b^2}{c d}$
By using concept of percentage error,
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\Delta P}{P} \% & =\frac{2 \Delta a}{a}+\frac{2 \Delta b}{b}+\frac{\Delta c}{c}+\frac{\Delta d}{d} \\
\therefore \quad \frac{\Delta P}{P} \% & =2 \times 2+2 \times 1+3+5 \\
& =4+2+3+5 \\
& =14 \%
\end{aligned}$

& = $\pm(2 \%+2 $\times$3 \%) \\
& = $\pm(2 \%+6 \%)= $\pm$8 \%

Assertion (A) The number 0.00764 has three significant figures.
Reason (R) If the number is less than 1 , the zeros on the right of the decimal point but to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant.
options: Both \((A)\) and \((R)\) are true and \((R)\) is the correct explanation of \((A)\).
Both \((A)\) and \((R)\) are true but \((R)\) is not the correct explanation of \((A)\).
questions.solution:
If the number is less than one, the zero on the right of decimal point but to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant, i.e. in \(\underline{\mathbf{0}} \underline{\underline{00} 764 $\text{, }$}\) the underlined zeroes are not significant. The number of significant digit is 3 .
Both assertion (A) and reason ( \($\mathrm{R}$ ) are correct and reason \((R)\) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

questions.q: If \(1 \%\) and \(2 \%\) are the errors in the measurement of mass and density of a cube respectively, then the error in the measurement of length is
questions.solution:
Given, error in measurement of mass,
\(\frac{\Delta m}{m}=$1 \%\)
and error in measurement of density, \(\frac{\Delta d}{d}=$2 \%\)
Now, density, \(d=\frac{\text{ mass }}{\text{ volume }} \Rightarrow$d=\frac{m}{V}\)
\(\therefore\) Volume of cube, \(V=l³\)
Then,
\(d=\frac{m}{l^3} \Rightarrow$l=$\left(\frac{m}{d}\right)$^{\frac{1}{3}}$\)
Then the error in measurement of length,
\$(\begin{aligned}$\frac{\Delta l}{l} \times$100 & =\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{\Delta m}{m} \times$100+\frac{\Delta d}{d} \times$100\right) \\
\frac{\Delta l}{l} \times$100 & =\frac{1}{3}(1+2) \times$100 \\
\frac{\Delta l}{l}$& =1 \%
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q:
Two resistance 60.36 W and 30.09 W are
connected in par al lel. The equiv a lent
resistance is
questions.solution:
Equivalent resistance is
$R_{\text{parallel }}=\frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1+R_2}=\frac{60 \times 30}{60+30}=20 \Omega$
and tolerance value is
$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \Delta R_P & =R_P\left\{\frac{\Delta R_1}{R_1}+\frac{\Delta R_2}{R_2}-\frac{\Delta R_1+\Delta R_2}{R_1+R_2}\right\} \\
& =20\left\{\frac{0.36}{60}+\frac{0.09}{30}-\frac{0.36+0.09}{90}\right\} \\
& =20\{0.006+0.003-0.005\}=0.085 \Omega
\end{aligned}$
So, resistance in parallel is $R_P=20 \pm 0.08$

questions.q: The work done in moving an object from origin to a point whose position vector is $\mathbf{r}=3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-5 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ by a force $\mathbf{F}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ is
questions.solution:
We know, work done $W=\mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{d}$
Given, force, $\mathbf{F}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$,
and position vector, $\mathbf{d}=3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-5 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Using vector identify $\hat{\mathbf{i}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{i}}=\hat{\mathbf{j}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{j}}=\hat{\mathbf{k}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{k}}=1$
Hence, $\mathbf{W}=\mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{d}=(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \cdot(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-5 \hat{\mathbf{k}})=6-2+5=9$ units

questions.q: In the measurement of a physical quantity $X=\frac{A^2 B}{C^{1 / 3} D^3}$. The percentage errors introduced in the measurements of the quantities $A, B, C$, and $D$ are $2 \%, 2 \%, 4 \%$ and $5 \%$, respectively. Then, the minimum amount of percentage error in the measurement of $X$ is contributed by
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& x=\frac{A^2 B}{C^{1 / 3} D^3} \\
& \% \text{ error in } x, \\
& \qquad \frac{\Delta x}{x}=2 \frac{\Delta A}{A}+\frac{\Delta B}{B}+\frac{1}{3} \frac{\Delta C}{C}+\frac{3 \Delta D}{D} \\
& 2\left(\frac{\Delta A}{A} \times 100 \%\right)+\left(\frac{\Delta B}{B} \times 100 \%\right) \\
& +\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{\Delta C}{C} \times 100 \%\right)+3\left(\frac{\Delta D}{D} \times 100 \%\right)
\end{aligned}$
Minimum percentage error
$=\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{\Delta C}{C} \times 100 \%\right)=\frac{1}{3} \times 4=1.1 \%$
